# Late-Round Flyers for 1 to 3 USD

**Summary.** Use at least three of our last four roster spots on 1 to 3 USD players who have a real path to starting minutes and a top 70 ceiling. The best fits are Porziņģis, Sheppard, Maluach, Claxton, Grimes and Santos. Players who only matter if someone else gets hurt belong on waivers in our league, and every flyer needs a minutes trigger and a cut date a few weeks into the season.

## The test: a role path and top 70 upside

Only take a flyer if there is a real chance he starts or wins a role. Before every 1 to 3 USD bid, ask one question: is he a starter now, or could he become one? If reports say he will not start, pass and keep the dollar. ([10-02](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=500), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=2322), [10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=1390))

The bar for upside is high. A late pick should have a top 70 ceiling. Ideally he can beat his draft spot by 40 to 50 places. In our 144-player draft, that means a player going near the cutoff needs a path into the top 100 or better. If a player's best case is his draft slot, he has no upside, and you can find him on waivers. ([10-01](https://youtu.be/EGdhmUgPAWY?t=1129), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2511), [09-07](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=2414), [09-17](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=1410))

Use minutes as the test. A guard or wing who gets about 27 minutes off the bench is enough for a late flyer. A big needs about 30 minutes. If his minutes get split down to about 22, he is useless. A starting center who gives FG%, blocks and rebounds is worth a late dollar even if the job may not last. Cheap centers like that are a good way to buy rebounds and blocks at the end of the auction. ([07-02](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=1334), [06-30](https://youtu.be/4GDfg2n2l8o?t=1075), [10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=804), [10-04](https://youtu.be/n4KkK-OJjqA?t=1139))

## Where the experts disagree: injury handcuffs

The experts split on backups who need an injury to someone else. One view says a backup who is one injury away from starting is a valid late flyer. The other view says counting on an injury is not enough, and players who only pay off if someone else gets hurt are poor late picks. ([10-02](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=2512), [10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=1390), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=2338))

Our rule: we have only 2 bench spots, and FAB waivers run every day. So leave pure handcuffs on waivers and bid the day the starter goes down. That covers Paul Reed behind Duren, Daniss Jenkins behind Cunningham, and Tari Eason behind Durant and Smith. The case is different when the starter is already out on draft day. Then the path is real. Gafford can start while Lively is out. Maluach can start while Mark Williams is out. Stewart starts if Edey's foot keeps him out. Check that news again just before 2026-10-18. ([Paul Reed](../profiles/players/paul-reed.md), [Daniss Jenkins](../profiles/players/daniss-jenkins.md), [Tari Eason](../profiles/players/tari-eason.md), [Daniel Gafford](../profiles/players/daniel-gafford.md), [Khaman Maluach](../profiles/players/khaman-maluach.md), [Isaiah Stewart](../profiles/players/isaiah-stewart.md))

## Best bets at the end of the auction

Porziņģis and Sheppard have the highest ceilings at this price. Porziņģis could be top 70 over about 40 games. Our league paid 21 USD for him last season, so do not let the room push him back toward that. Our 4 IL slots make him easy to hold. Sheppard has top 40 to 50 upside if he starts. He fills threes, steals and blocks without a weak category. ([Kristaps Porziņģis](../profiles/players/kristaps-porzingis.md), [Reed Sheppard](../profiles/players/reed-sheppard.md))

The cheap centers fit the starting-center rule. Claxton is worth up to about 3 USD if he starts near 30 minutes. Maluach's ceiling is the top 75 if he starts over Ighodaro. Experts call Poeltl's 2 USD market value too low. ([Nic Claxton](../profiles/players/nic-claxton.md), [Khaman Maluach](../profiles/players/khaman-maluach.md), [Jakob Poeltl](../profiles/players/jakob-poeltl.md), [10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=804))

On the wings, Grimes is a likely starter at 1 USD and has no weak category. Santos is a 1 USD bet that experts see reaching the top 70 after the trade deadline, as long as the Golden State role holds. ([Quentin Grimes](../profiles/players/quentin-grimes.md), [Gui Santos](../profiles/players/gui-santos.md))

## Draft pairs, not singles

Most late flyers miss. Taking two players in a similar spot raises the odds that one of them hits. When two players fight for the same job, draft both, see who wins, and cut the other. ([09-07](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=1934), [09-10](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=1799), [08-24](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=2388), [09-04](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=479))

Three pairs fit our auction. Santos and Lendeborg compete for Golden State minutes while Butler is out, and Santos's own note says to draft Lendeborg as the hedge. Grimes and Mamukelashvili compete for the open Lakers starting spots. In Dallas, Gafford is the 1 USD pick while Lively is out. Morez Johnson is the waiver follow-up if Dusty May starts him over Gafford. ([Gui Santos](../profiles/players/gui-santos.md), [Yaxel Lendeborg](../profiles/players/yaxel-lendeborg.md), [Quentin Grimes](../profiles/players/quentin-grimes.md), [Sandro Mamukelashvili](../profiles/players/sandro-mamukelashvili.md), [Daniel Gafford](../profiles/players/daniel-gafford.md), [Morez Johnson Jr.](../profiles/players/morez-johnson.md))

## Budget, timing and drop rules

Price decides whether an upside pick makes sense. The same player can be a fade early and a fine swing late. A flyer that fails at 1 to 3 USD costs almost nothing and does not ruin a draft. Plan to fill at least three of your last four roster spots with flyers. That means about 4 to 12 USD in total, so keep that money in reserve while you buy your core. ([10-01](https://youtu.be/aLP080hxizA?t=1729), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2511), [10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=1499), [10-04](https://youtu.be/n4KkK-OJjqA?t=1698))

Write down each flyer's trigger before the draft. That can be a starting job, a minutes number, or a teammate's return date. Check it in the first weeks. Late picks are often drops, and you take them to learn what their role turns out to be. If the trigger has not happened by about week 3, cut him and use one of the 6 weekly acquisitions on a waiver player. Mikel Brown is the one exception. If he starts, hold him until about Thanksgiving. ([08-23](https://youtu.be/hm5-fiCa5S4?t=2248), [09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=1431), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=2517), [10-02](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=1128), [Mikel Brown Jr.](../profiles/players/mikel-brown.md))

Young players need care. Uncertain rookies belong in the flyer zone, and experts lean toward second-year players over third-year players. But second-year flyers drafted at 101 to 150 reach the top 100 only 13% of the time. Undrafted sophomores almost never matter. Playoff schedules matter too. Houston plays only 10 games in our playoff weeks, which gives less reason to hold Sheppard, VanVleet or Eason if they start slow. ([06-25](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=867), [09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=481), [09-04](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=423), [Reed Sheppard](../profiles/players/reed-sheppard.md), [Fred VanVleet](../profiles/players/fred-vanvleet.md), [Tari Eason](../profiles/players/tari-eason.md))
